The NAICS for this requirement is 541611 Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services, and the Product Service Code (PSC) is R425. The period of performance will include a base period and two, 12-month option periods beginning on or about September 4, 2026. The place of performance is at the vendor�s facility and various military installations. Description of Requirement The Defense Suicide Prevention Office (DSPO) requires a non-personal services Contractor to review, tailor, update, expand, and validate the Connect Program, previously known as the Wingman Guardian Connect Program, for the Department of War (DoW) and all Military Services (Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, National Guard Bureau, and Coast Guard). The Contractor shall validate the implementation of the Connect Program and provide a report that includes evaluation findings and recommendations for sustained program implementation and evaluation. The Connect Program (Wyman et al 2020; 2022) provides group interactive training for military personnel, followed by text messages and base-wide activities to embed concepts into culture and peer networks. The Connect Program�s interactive group design progresses from individual engagement (e.g., each participant shares career goals and values) to building group-level skills and norms (e.g., mapping group strengths). Specifically, participants learn together about and model skills to each other to grow and sustain �Four Cores� supportive of mental health and essential to job success: Kinship, Purpose, Guidance, and Balance. The vendor is required to have a sublicense for the Connect Program in order to tailor, update, and expand the Program. Justification for Noncompetitive Action The Connect Program is the only developed and tested community-based suicide prevention training program to achieve a Gold-Standard conducting randomized controlled trials with (1,500 Air Force) active U.S. military personnel that demonstrated significant reductions in suicide risk, depressive symptoms, and occupational problems where participants showed improved mental health outcomes. To achieve a Gold-Standard, a company must demonstrate a framework of rigorous, transparent, and ethical practices that ensure its findings are tested, valid, reproducible, and trustworthy. The Connect Program is the only community-based suicide prevention program with this level of evidence. It has taken several years for the Connect Program to conduct the trials and obtain the adoption needed for the Gold Standard. SafeSide Prevention, LLC is uniquely qualified as the only company that is sublicensed by Connect Media LLC to deliver and scale the Connect Program with fidelity and has a proven ability to adapt the program to new military and civilian markets. According to the market research, no other entity is granted sublicensing rights to the Connect Program nor will Connect Media LLC be issuing other sublicenses. Therefore, no other vendors can fulfill this requirement. As part of the market research, the Government communicated with the University of Rochester and Connect Media LLC, who holds perpetual, worldwide Copyright License, and were notified in writing by Connect Media LLC that no other vendors will be granted sublicensing rights to the Connect Program. The University of Rochester and Connect Media LLC provided the Government copies of their licenses, sublicense, and copyright agreements.
